Netanyahu reportedly tells aides renewed war with Iran 'unavoidable' as Trump weighs options

Channel 13 reported Wednesday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told top ministers and security officials that "an operation against Iran is unavoidable." He is reportedly pushing Trump to join a days-long war.

An unnamed senior IDF officer said the Israeli military and US Central Command have "shared and approved plans," and that "the question is the timing." Both sides are waiting for a Trump decision.

Axios reported Thursday that Trump, who last week called new strikes "quite unlikely," has asked the Pentagon and intelligence agencies to assess how Iran would respond to CENTCOM attack scenarios. The White House also asked whether an operation could avoid large-scale Iranian attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure.

CENTCOM chief Adm. Brad Cooper met IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir and other Israeli security officials, including Mossad chief Roman Gofman, before travelling to Saudi Arabia.

Earlier reports said Zamir was the only top security official opposed to an immediate resumption of strikes. Netanyahu lost his parliamentary majority in the October 27 Knesset election.

At the IAEA board meeting, the US, UK, France and Germany accused Iran of "stonewalling" on inspections. Inspectors have not accessed the nuclear sites bombed in June 2025, and Iran's stock of highly enriched uranium remains unaccounted for.
